criteria.text: n2 = matches whose BOTH order votes changed between passes, against the EXACT CONDITIONAL NULL given T (uniform T-subsets of the 600 cells; 10^6 draws, seed 42). At T = 59 the two-sided alpha-0.05 rejection region is n2 >= 7 (P0 0.0146); NO lower region exists (P0(n2 = 0) = 0.042). HELD (i.i.d. per-call model consistent; the canary pattern is forced arithmetic) iff n2 outside the region; FAILED (within-match dependence) iff inside. The count is the statistic; no interval clause. SCOREABLE (MDE about 6.4 double changes above the null mean 2.86 at DEFF 1.09; prediction 10).
criteria.value: n2 = 10 against E0 2.856, SD0 1.528, P0(n2 >= 10) = 0.0001 (region >= 7); [QUALIFIED 2026-09-23 by the registrar on the post-run review 64bdecb (D-1 HIGH)]: C1 rejects independent change at ONE COMMON per-call rate. It shows MATCH-LEVEL CO-CHANGE: change propensity is a match-level quantity. It does NOT separate dependence of the two calls GIVEN the match from HETEROGENEITY of change rates across matches: with 2 cells per match and one retest the two are observationally equivalent. Stratified by the pass-1 TIE / decisive state (per-cell change 0.307 vs 0.029), n2 = 10 lies OUTSIDE the stratified region (p 0.103); likewise by pass-1 configuration (p 0.145) and by pass-2 state (p 0.057); a two-class mixture reproduces the 251 / 39 / 10 distribution exactly. The outcome file's reading 'within-match dependence ... a property of the judge on these matches' claims more than C1 licenses and is superseded by this bracket. The 3-event excess in the pass-1-decisive stratum ((A,A) -> (TIE,TIE), P0 0.0003) is UNREGISTERED and DESCRIPTIVE: a lead, never a finding; so are the position-preference co-swaps (4 of 6).

plain_description.what: In a repeated judge run (300 matches, each judged in both answer orders, run twice), it counts how often both order votes of a match changed together. It compares this with what independent random vote changes would predict. No calls.
plain_description.why: Checks whether "retest changes only happen at ties" is just arithmetic from independent per-call noise, which would justify computing match-level noise floors from a single per-call rate.
plain_description.information: If independence held, noise floors could be derived cheaply. Result: it failed. Both votes changed together 10 times against about 3 expected, so changes cluster within matches. No match-level noise floor may be derived from one pooled per-call rate. It cannot tell real within-match dependence apart from some matches simply being shakier. No recorded number moves. Older judged question family, later ruled 'history, not evidence'.
